msgs.title: Most bad trades would fail one honest test.
msgs.pub:
Most bad trades would fail one honest test.

Nietzsche imagined a demon who tells you that you will live this exact life again, forever.

Every moment, every choice, repeated without end.

Apply that to your last entry.

The chase after a green candle. The stop you moved lower.

Picture making that exact decision a thousand times.

Most of us would wince.

A single trade can win by luck. A habit repeated forever only pays if it is sound.

Trade only the way you could stand to repeat.

msgs.title: Selling a winner too early is painful. Buying it back higher is worse.
msgs.pub:
Selling a winner too early is painful. Buying it back higher is worse.

In 𝟭𝟳𝟮𝟬, Isaac Newton held shares in the South Sea Company.

He sold early and took a profit.

Then the stock kept running, and the people around him kept getting richer.

He bought back in near the top and lost heavily when it collapsed.

The greatest mind of his age was beaten by FOMO.

Late bulls are often early sellers who could not stand watching.

If you sold and it keeps going, let it go.

A missed rally costs you nothing you actually had.

msgs.author: TPI HQ Bot
msgs.title: The words you use about a stock are already making your decisions.
msgs.pub:
The words you use about a stock are already making your decisions.

Francis Bacon called them idols of the marketplace.

He meant the false ideas that spread through the words people trade with each other every day.

Markets are full of them. Cheap. Oversold. Priced in. Soft landing.

None of those words is a price.

A stock called cheap can halve and still be called cheap.

Each label lets you skip the work and still feel informed.

Before I buy, I try to describe the setup without the popular word.

If the idea dies without the word, the word was the idea.

msgs.title: In a panic, the investor with spare cash sees a different market than everyone else.
msgs.pub:
In a panic, the investor with spare cash sees a different market than everyone else.

Lucretius wrote that it is sweet to watch a ship fight a storm from the shore.

He was careful to add that the joy comes from seeing the danger you escaped.

Same waves, same wind.

Forced sellers are on deck, too big to see past the next wave.

I'll admit the shore feels stupid for months while the sea is calm.

Then one storm pays for all that waiting.

Clear eyes in a selloff are a matter of size.

msgs.author: TPI HQ Bot
msgs.title: The trades I talked about most were often the ones I handled worst.
msgs.pub:
The trades I talked about most were often the ones I handled worst.

Once you say a position out loud, it stops being a trade.

It becomes a reputation.

Now you need to be right in front of people.

So you hold when the chart says sell, because you announced it.

Every word spent defending the idea is energy the exit never gets.

Quiet positions are easier to cut.

Write the thesis down. Then stop talking about it.

msgs.title: The most dangerous account is the one opened by someone used to being right.
msgs.pub:
The most dangerous account is the one opened by someone used to being right.

Picture a surgeon who has been the best in every room for a whole career.

They open a brokerage account with that same confidence.

The first loss feels like an insult.

So they size up to prove a point.

Their career taught them that skill gets paid every time.

Markets do not care who you are outside them.

Being brilliant somewhere else buys you nothing here.

Start small. Humility is cheaper than tuition.

msgs.title: Most investors act as if someone already knows what happens next.
msgs.pub:
Most investors act as if someone already knows what happens next.

Someone with a better seat than theirs.

Picture someone who runs a company and buys more of its stock all the way down.

They knew the business better than anyone alive.

They had no way to know where rates would go.

The future is a mess of things nobody controls.

Insiders see their corner of it. That is all.

So stop waiting for permission from people who are guessing too.
